key_insight: Latent World Recovery (LWR) tackles missing-modality learning by first aligning each modality into a shared latent space, then building a unified representation only from the modalities available at inference time. This lets multimodal systems remain useful even when some inputs are absent.
problem_solved: The paper addresses multimodal learning in settings where not all modalities are available when a prediction must be made, which is common in bioscience and other real-world applications.
method: Learn modality-specific embeddings and align them into a common latent space.
Fuse only the embeddings from modalities that are actually present to form a unified representation.
Use the recovered latent representation for downstream prediction, enabling robustness to missing inputs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to deploy multimodal models in messy real-world settings where data completeness cannot be guaranteed. It improves robustness and makes multimodal systems more usable in domains like biomedicine, where partial observations are the norm.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multiple modalities entering separate encoders and merging into a shared latent space.
An availability mask graphic highlighting which modalities are present vs. missing at inference time.
A before/after comparison chart showing standard multimodal fusion versus LWR under missing data.
Icons representing different bioscience modalities (e.g., imaging, genomics, clinical data).
paper_title: Latent World Recovery for Multimodal Learning with Missing Modalities
paper_authors: Hui Wang, Tianyu Ren, Joseph Butler, Christopher Baker, Karen Rafferty
